title: Extract a long filter lambda into a named rule

blocks.text: A `filter` lambda with five `if` statements in it is a puzzle. Moving the rules into a named method turns the pipeline into a sentence: `filter(ItemRules::isValidItem)`.

The file declares `enum Status { ACTIVE, DELETED }`, `record Owner(String name, boolean verified)` and `record Item(String id, int value, boolean active, Status status, Owner owner)`. Write two static methods of `ItemRules`:

items: `boolean isValidItem(Item item)`: the item is not `null`, its value is above zero, it is active, its status is not `DELETED`, and it has an owner who is verified.
`List<String> validIds(List<Item> items)`: the ids of the valid items, in order, using `isValidItem` as a method reference.

blocks.text: Every rule on the page's list counts, including the ones about things that may be missing.

cases.says: Only active, positive, undeleted items with a verified owner are kept, in order.
A null item is simply not valid; it never throws.
An item whose owner is null is not valid; it never throws.
An item with status DELETED is not valid, whatever else holds.
A value must be above zero; zero itself is not valid.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A lambda with several rules in it is extracted to a named method and passed as a method reference.
